subject: Compact Compute pack selection, committed discount pathway and rollback clause
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbushealth.com>

Cc: Paul Gomez <paul.gomez@nimbushealth.com>, procure@nimbushealth.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compact pack — questions on pricing bands and rollout

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our engineering lead liked the latency profile on the Compact Compute configuration. We're trying to nail down packaging before procurement kicks off. A few specific asks:

- We anticipate starting with ~75k tokens/month (pilot) and scaling to ~600k tokens/month within 6 months. What tier on Redwood maps best to that growth curve?
- Does Redwood have a defined "compact" pack that bundles compute and KV cache optimizations? If so, what's included vs standard Starter/Dedicated tiers?
- Pricing: what discount bands do you offer for a firm 12-month committed spend? Our procurement target is to get to an annualized discount >15% (net). Is that feasible?
- Contract: we need a rollback/usage clause in case our usage falls below 50% of committed for two consecutive months — what's the standard language?

I've attached an early SOW for procurement as a starting point (Nimbus_SOW_v0.1.docx). Can you loop in any legal or CS folks we should expect to see on the SOW?

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of Platform
Nimbus Health
(attachment: Nimbus_SOW_v0.1.docx)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Paul Gomez <paul.gomez@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compact pack — questions on pricing bands and rollout

Sarah — appreciate the clear ask and the SOW. Short answers up front, then details.

- Tier recommendation: Compact Compute Pack (our 3rd tier) — optimized for medium burst workloads, includes prefix KV caching up to 32GB and continuous-batching defaults for sub-200ms p95 on T4/RTX-class hardware.
- What's in the bundle: token throughput SLA, 24/7 support for production routes, ON-DEMAND quantization profile, and one onboarding engagement (4 weeks). Not all features in Dedicated (e.g., private plane routing) are in the Compact pack by default.
- Discounts for annual commit: we offer a sliding scale. Typical bands are 5% (monthly), 12% (6-month commit), 18% (12-month commit) — however, commercial approval is required for anything >15% on initial quote.
- Rollback language: standard is a 30-day notice period and an automatic re-rate to the next lower price band if usage <50% for two consecutive months; we can add a one-time cure period where credits are applied. Legal will need to formalize.

I've attached a high-level pricing model for the Compact pack for your expected growth curve (pricing_model_v2.xlsx).

Next steps I suggest: I can loop in Markus (sales director) to approve the 18% band for a firm 12-month commit, and Monica (CS) to scope onboarding credits and an implementation timeline. If that sounds good I'll prepare an updated SOW + redlines for your procurement team.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

If Markus can confirm commercial flexibility on the discount band and Monica can confirm onboarding credits, we can present to procurement next Wednesday.

Rachel / Monica — I can approve the 18% net discount for the 12-month committed spend with the following commercial guardrails:

- Commitment triggers: 12-month minimum term with a minimum monthly committed token burn (we'll specify exact token floor in the term sheet).
- Rollback: acceptable to set the threshold at 60% for two consecutive months. If usage falls below the threshold we revert pricing to the standard Compact list for the remainder of the term.
- Cure/credit: offer a one-time credit equal to 25% of the monthly difference between committed and actual usage, applied once during months 3–6 as a cure. After that, the re-rate stands.
- On-prem add-on: treat as a separate line item priced by engineering; Monica, can you confirm estimate and whether PHI routing requires Redwood Private?

I've attached a short discount term sheet so we have language to feed legal (discount_term_sheet.pdf). Once legal signs off we can send a redlined SOW + DocuSign.

-Markus
